title: Crushing chest pain at the dacha
presenting_complaint: Central crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw for 50 minutes, started while chopping wood. Sweaty, nauseated, vomited once.
history: Brought by ambulance. Type 2 diabetes on metformin, hypertension on ramipril, smokes 20 cigarettes per day. No prior myocardial infarction. No recent surgery or bleeding, no history of stroke.

findings.name: 12-lead ECG
findings.value: sinus bradycardia; ST elevation 3 mm in II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL

findings.name: Chest X-ray
findings.value: normal heart size, no pulmonary oedema

diagnosis_options.label: Acute inferior STEMI with right ventricular involvement
diagnosis_options.explanation: ST elevation in II, III and aVF with reciprocal depression in I and aVL, plus ST elevation in V4R and hypotension with raised JVP, indicate an acute inferior STEMI with right ventricular infarction.

diagnosis_options.label: NSTEMI
diagnosis_options.explanation: Partially right: this is an acute myocardial infarction, but the persistent ST elevation defines STEMI rather than NSTEMI.

diagnosis_options.label: Aortic dissection
diagnosis_options.explanation: Considered as a differential, but the ECG pattern of inferior ST elevation with RV involvement and the clinical picture fit an inferior STEMI; no supporting features of dissection are given.

diagnosis_options.label: Acute pericarditis
diagnosis_options.explanation: Considered as a differential; pericarditis typically gives diffuse ST elevation without reciprocal depression or territorial distribution, unlike this case.

diagnosis_options.label: Pulmonary embolism
diagnosis_options.explanation: Considered as a differential; the inferior ST elevation with right ventricular lead involvement and raised JVP with clear lungs are explained by right ventricular infarction rather than PE.

management_options.label: Aspirin 300 mg loading dose
management_options.explanation: Essential antiplatelet therapy in acute STEMI.

management_options.label: Immediate transfer for primary PCI
management_options.explanation: Essential reperfusion strategy for acute STEMI.

management_options.label: IV fluid bolus for hypotension
management_options.explanation: Essential: the right ventricular infarct is preload-dependent, so volume loading supports cardiac output and blood pressure.

management_options.label: P2Y12 inhibitor loading (ticagrelor or clopidogrel)
management_options.explanation: Reasonable and indicated as part of dual antiplatelet therapy, though less immediately critical than aspirin and reperfusion.

management_options.label: Sublingual nitroglycerin
management_options.explanation: Harmful here: nitrates precipitate profound hypotension in right ventricular infarction.

management_options.label: Morphine as first-line analgesia
management_options.explanation: Avoid: harmful in this setting, as it can worsen hypotension in right ventricular infarction.
